blocks.text:
The itinerary leaves room between long journeys, so the trip does not become a constant rush. In Rio, there is time between excursions to enjoy the hotel and the ocean. In the Amazon, you stay at Mirante do Gavião on the banks of the Rio Negro, close to the Anavilhanas archipelago. After the busier days, the final 4 days are set aside for Muro Alto beach.

## Accommodation along the route

In Rio, you will spend 4 nights at **Copacabana Palace**, in a **One Bedroom Double Suite** with a pool view and breakfast included. The hotel faces Copacabana, across Avenida Atlântica from the ocean.

At Iguazu, you will stay at **Belmond Hotel das Cataratas**, in a **Deluxe** double room with breakfast. The hotel is inside the national park, facing the falls.

In the Amazon, you will stay at **Mirante do Gavião Amazon Lodge** near Novo Airão, in a **Deluxe** room on a full-board basis. The lodge has a pier, the Camu Camu restaurant, a swimming pool and terraces overlooking the Rio Negro and the Anavilhanas islands.

The beach stay is at **Nannai Muro Alto**, in a double bungalow with a sea view. Half board is included in your accommodation. The hotel is right on the beachfront at Muro Alto.

## What makes this route special

Rio offers more than a brief round of its main sights on this itinerary. Over 5 days, you can see the city from above, explore the historic centre, spend a day on the water near Ilha Grande and leave time for your own plans. This pace suits a longer trip: after each busy day, you can return to Copacabana Palace, relax by the pool or walk to the ocean without another transfer.

Sugar Loaf reveals the city from the bay. The cable car first climbs to Urca, then to the upper viewing platform. Corcovado gives you a different perspective: the train passes through the Tijuca Forest, and from the viewpoint you can see how the neighbourhoods fit between the mountains, bay and ocean. The two viewpoints complement each other and help you understand Rio's geography.

The day at Ilha Grande takes you from the city to the sea. A private boat travels between the islands and stops in bays. In some places the water is calm and clear; elsewhere the forest almost reaches the beach. You can swim, look out for sea turtles and dolphins, and spend several hours without a packed sightseeing schedule.

New Year's Eve is a separate part of the journey. The day before the celebrations is free, followed by a VIP dinner at Belmond before you head to Copacabana. White clothes, flowers for Iemanjá, concert stages and fireworks over the sea create a scene very different from an ordinary evening in Rio. After midnight, many people go down to the water and jump over 7 waves while making wishes.

At Iguazu, staying close to the falls is central to the experience. Belmond Hotel das Cataratas is inside the national park, so the surroundings become quieter after the park closes. The next day, the Brazilian trail gradually takes you towards the Devil's Throat: first you see individual cascades, then the whole canyon opens up, and finally the mist and roar of the water become part of the walk itself.

For more action, there is the Macuco Safari. After a journey through the forest and a short walk, you board a boat that heads towards the cascades. The Bird Park offers a different experience, with large aviaries of toucans, macaws and ibises. A flight over Iguazu lets you see the river, the line of waterfalls and the forest on both sides of the border at once.

The Amazon section begins after your flight to Manaus and the transfer to Novo Airão. Here, the journey centres on the Rio Negro. Mirante do Gavião is close to Anavilhanas, so in the morning you can set off directly from the lodge to the islands and communities, returning in the evening to the pier, swimming pool and restaurant.

Anavilhanas is a network of dark channels between long, forested islands. Your day on the water includes visits to the communities of Santo Antônio and Tiririca, a forest walk, a traditional lunch, a beach and the giant Macucu tree. On the return journey, there is a chance to see pink dolphins.

The next day can include two more experiences characteristic of the Amazon. The first is a close encounter with pink dolphins near Novo Airão. The second is a trip to the meeting of the Rio Negro and Solimões, where dark and light-brown waters flow side by side for several kilometres, retaining their different colours and temperatures.

After the Amazon, the route changes again. Porto de Galinhas brings you back to the ocean, away from the city setting of Copacabana. Muro Alto is sheltered by a reef wall, making the water calmer, and natural pools appear at low tide. You can plan these 4 days around the tides: head to the water in the morning, relax by the swimming pool during the day, and, if you wish, take a jangada raft trip, go on a buggy ride or dive.

## Travel logistics

The journey includes several flights and long road transfers, so flight times matter. For the group transfer from Manaus to Mirante do Gavião, you need to arrive before 15:00; on the return journey, your flight from Manaus must depart after 14:30. Other schedules require a separate private transfer. For the beach stay, there is a drive of about 60 km from Recife to Porto de Galinhas. On the final day, you travel via Recife back to Rio, where you make your own connection to your international flight.

Domestic flights are not included in the basic tour price. The indicative cost starts at USD 1,050 per person for the route Rio – Manaus – Iguazu – Recife/Noronha – Rio. Additional helicopter and seaplane flights are also charged separately.
